meta.scope: AD forest recovery only — domain controllers and core AD services (FSMO, replication, SYSVOL, DNS). Does not automate credential hygiene (KRBTGT rotation, privileged account resets, service account resets) or dependent service restoration (ADFS, Azure AD Connect, PKI, LDAP-dependent applications).
meta.notes: Phase baseline ranges calibrated against AD recovery engagement data. Ranges are [conservative_hours, aggressive_hours]. Expected = midpoint.

small.label: Small
small.description: Up to 5 domain controllers · Single domain · 1–3 office locations

medium.label: Medium
medium.description: 6–20 domain controllers · Up to 3 domains · 4–10 locations

limited.label: Limited
limited.description: No documented recovery runbook · Backups rarely or never tested · Fewer than 2 staff with AD recovery experience

developing.label: Developing
developing.description: Some recovery documentation · Backups tested more than a year ago · 1–2 experienced staff

mature.label: Mature
mature.description: Documented runbook · Backup restore tested within the last year · 3+ experienced staff

phases.label: Containment & Decision to Restore
phases.description: Isolating affected systems and deciding on restore vs. rebuild path

phases.label: Restore Domain Controllers
phases.description: Building a clean recovery environment and restoring domain controllers from backup

phases.label: Re-establish Core AD Services
phases.description: Restoring FSMO roles, AD replication, SYSVOL, and DNS so the directory is operational

phases.label: Credential Hygiene
phases.description: Resetting privileged accounts, service accounts, and rotating KRBTGT — required after every forest recovery. Not automated by Identity Recovery; time is identical with or without the tool.

phases.label: Validation & AD Operational
phases.description: Confirming AD is healthy and handing off to teams to begin restoring dependent services

low.label: Low
low.description: ~once per 50 years · Strong security posture, mature controls

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.description: ~once per 20 years · Average enterprise risk profile

elevated.label: Elevated
elevated.description: ~once per 10 years · Known gaps or prior AD incidents

high.label: High
high.description: ~once per 5 years · Active threat exposure or recent breach
